nodes.name: Existing table pretrained models require fine-tuning
nodes.description: Pre-trained neural networks that jointly model column names and table entries must be fine-tuned to bring benefits, lacking the convenience of popular foundation models in text or vision.

nodes.name: Existing models have sizeable computation costs
nodes.description: Existing table foundation models come with sizeable computation costs and cannot easily be reused or combined with other architectures; Kim et al. (2024) report times 200x slower than XGBoost.

nodes.name: TARTE proposal
nodes.description: TARTE is introduced as a foundation model that transforms tables to knowledge-enhanced vector representations using strings to capture semantics.

nodes.name: TARTE representations reusable without fine-tuning
nodes.description: TARTE yields representations that facilitate subsequent learning with little additional cost, unlike prior models where benefits come mainly from fine-tuning rather than pre-training.

nodes.name: Column-cell pair modeling via language model
nodes.description: TARTE models a row as a set of column(E)-cell(X) pairs, mapping column names, numerical, categorical, and datetime values to the same dimension using a language model and datetime converter.

nodes.name: TARTE avoids CARTE's graph structure
nodes.description: TARTE avoids the graph structure used in CARTE, which creates a bottleneck limiting information flow between inputs in self-attention layers.

nodes.name: TARTE keeps all relations in single attention mechanism
nodes.description: By avoiding the graph structure, TARTE keeps all column relations in a single attention mechanism, providing better context to capture data semantics.

nodes.name: Shallow three-layer architecture
nodes.description: TARTE is trained as a shallow architecture of three layers, reflecting that the input works in a column-level setting prone to oversmoothing with deeper architectures.

nodes.name: YAGO4.5 lacks numerical diversity
nodes.description: YAGO4.5 includes relatively little numerical information compared to downstream tables and lacks diversity in relational information, especially for numerical triples.

nodes.name: Enrichment with Wikidata
nodes.description: TARTE enriches YAGO4.5 with numerical facts (numbers and dates) from the more comprehensive but noisier Wikidata to address its numerical information shortcomings.

nodes.name: Combined knowledge base scale
nodes.description: The resulting combined knowledge base describes over 5.5 million entities and includes 30 million facts with 687 distinct relations.

nodes.name: Contrastive pre-training with positive/negative sampling
nodes.description: TARTE is pre-trained using contrastive learning with in-batch negatives, where positive samples are generated by replacing one or two facts with different information.

nodes.name: TARTE post-training paradigms
nodes.description: TARTE facilitates learning via various post-training paradigms: fine-tuning, use as a frozen featurizer, or combination with other models via boosting.

nodes.name: Boosting strategy
nodes.description: The base tabular model with the original table is ensembled with a model that fits the train residuals using TARTE embedded features.

nodes.name: Domain specialization via boosting
nodes.description: Domain specialized representations, extracted from fine-tuned models of related tables, can be incorporated with the boosting strategy by sequentially fitting residuals with domain-specialized representations.

nodes.name: TARTE avoids costly joint learning
nodes.description: TARTE avoids the costly joint-learning required by CARTE, and can readily extract embeddings from fine-tuned models of related tables for domain specialization.

nodes.name: TARTE variants best on small tables
nodes.description: On small tables (n=32 to 1024), pre-trained models generally perform better, with variants of TARTE as the best performing models regardless of sample size.

nodes.name: TARTE and TabPFNv2 form Pareto frontier
nodes.description: Considering computation-time trade-offs, variants of TARTE and TabPFNv2 form the Pareto frontier on small tables.

nodes.name: Boosting improves prediction with better pre-training
nodes.description: Boosting a base model with pre-trained embeddings improves prediction, and because TARTE is better pre-trained, its embeddings complement base models better than CARTE's.

nodes.name: TARTE-FT has high computation burden
nodes.description: TARTE-FT does not require a strong base tabular model but comes with computation burdens due to extensive hyperparameter tuning.

nodes.name: TARTE helps on larger tables
nodes.description: On larger tables (n=10,000), pre-training schemes remain the Pareto frontier, with TARTE-FT and TARTE-B outperforming baselines.

nodes.name: Fine-tuning TARTE has heavy runtime cost
nodes.description: Fine-tuning TARTE brings more prediction benefits at larger n, but at a heavy cost with a 14-fold runtime increase compared to TARTE-B-TabPFNv2.

nodes.name: TARTE-B-TabPFNv2 gives performance and scalability
nodes.description: TARTE-B-TabPFNv2 gives both performance and scalability, improving over TabVec-TabPFNv2 at a small compute cost.

nodes.name: FastText importance for TARTE performance
nodes.description: Comparing MinHash to TARTE reveals the importance of FastText, since it captures semantic similarities that combine with the transformer architecture to form an inductive bias of smoothness.

nodes.name: CARTE without fine-tuning underperforms random weights
nodes.description: For CARTE representations used without fine-tuning, pre-trained representations perform less well compared to random weights regardless of pre-train data, showing these representations lack out-of-the-box reusability.

nodes.name: Enriched YAGO4.5 improves knowledge pre-training
nodes.description: A proper combination of pre-train data (Enriched YAGO4.5), architecture, and preprocessing improves knowledge pre-training performance for TARTE.

nodes.name: TARTE pre-training schemes on CARTE underperform TARTE
nodes.description: Applying TARTE's pre-training schemes (New Sampling) to CARTE's architecture helps but does not match TARTE's own performance, highlighting multiple sources of improvement in TARTE beyond just the pre-training scheme.

nodes.name: Long string entries limit TARTE benefit
nodes.description: TARTE works less well on tables with long string entries, likely a limitation of FastText embeddings.

nodes.name: Inlier probability increases TARTE benefit
nodes.description: TARTE brings more benefits for tables with many strings considered inliers to the pre-training source, showing the need for pretraining to cover downstream terminology well.

nodes.name: TARTE benefits from complex tables
nodes.description: Overall, TARTE brings benefits on more complex tables with many complex strings, particularly when those strings resemble strings seen during pre-training.

nodes.name: TARTE reuses domain-specialized models efficiently
nodes.description: TARTE can readily reuse domain-specialized models for a new target table, amortizing training cost, unlike baselines that require refitting.

nodes.name: TARTE efficient with multiple sources
nodes.description: With multiple source tables, TARTE's runtime is dominated by the training time of source tables, whereas CARTE-MT requires pairwise fitting for each source, markedly increasing compute costs.

nodes.name: TARTE-B-TabPFNv2 best domain specialization result
nodes.description: TARTE-B-TabPFNv2 gives the best predictions among domain specialization approaches, benefiting from blending inference from the target table with source-tuned representations.

isolated_nodes.name: Tree-based models lead start on tabular data
isolated_nodes.description: Tree-based models have historically had a lead start for tabular learning due to their inductive biases matching properties of tabular data.

isolated_nodes.name: TabPFN prior fitted network approach
isolated_nodes.description: TabPFN pre-trains a prior fitted network over many synthetic datasets, performing in-context prediction using the training set as context in a transformer forward pass.

isolated_nodes.name: LLMs as tabular learners via row-to-text conversion
isolated_nodes.description: LLMs can be adapted to tables by turning rows into sentences, with dedicated fine-tuning turning them into best performers in very few-shot settings.

isolated_nodes.name: Model specifications
isolated_nodes.description: TARTE's transformer has three self-attention layers with 24 multi-head attentions, 768 hidden dimension, 2048 feed-forward dimension, and over 25 million trainable parameters.

isolated_nodes.name: Benchmark datasets
isolated_nodes.description: The empirical study uses 40 regression and 11 classification datasets from the CARTE benchmark, plus nine TabLLM datasets with higher fractions of numerical columns.

isolated_nodes.name: TabLLM comparison result
isolated_nodes.description: On datasets with more numerical columns and lower-cardinality categorical columns from TabLLM, TabPFN tends to perform better, but TARTE-B can still help base models.

isolated_nodes.name: Table understanding vs tabular learning distinction
isolated_nodes.description: Table understanding models leverage world knowledge via LLM-style in-context learning, whereas tabular learning models require post-training further from next-token prediction and often need to aggregate information across many rows.

structural_reasoning: The graph captures the paper's full narrative arc: motivation for a reusable knowledge-pretrained table model (C1), architectural design choices distinguishing TARTE from CARTE (C2), the knowledge base construction and contrastive pretraining procedure (C3), the post-training/reuse mechanisms including boosting and domain specialization (C4), and extensive empirical validation across small tables (C5), large tables (C6), ablations isolating the sources of TARTE's benefit (C7), which downstream tables benefit most (C8), and domain-specialization efficiency (C9). These components map cleanly onto the paper's section structure and show strong internal coherence with mostly majority/unanimous-confidence edges. Background material on prior work (TabPFN, LLM-based tabular learners) and setup details remain appropriately isolated as context. A few results-section edges rely on single-run inference since empirical claims are often presented as parallel findings rather than explicit causal statements.
